title.narrative: Food Security Portal Phase III

description.narrative: The Food Security Portal was created in 2011 by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI). Its aim is to address the shortage of easily accessible and relevant data at global level and to support and inform global food security discussions by making news, data, tools, and price analysis more accessible to a wide range of users.

title.narrative: Number of people in situations of food crisis in countries of subSaharan Africa.

description.narrative: Number of people in situations of food crisis in countries of subSaharan Africa.

comment.narrative: Target Visible reduction

In 2019 according to the 2020 Global Report on Food Crisis an estimated 135 million people around the world faced acute level of hunger. At that time the number reflected the highest level of acute hunger since the reports inception in 2017. In 2020 the COVID19 pandemic and the associated policy responses had wideranging impacts across the globe in terms of health food security incomes and livelihoods and access to critical services. According to the 2021 Global Report on Food Crises the number of people facing severe food insecurity went up to at least 155 million people in 2020. The combination of conflict climate change and economic shocks which were further exacerbated by the impacts of the COVID19 pandemic pushed the number of acutely food insecure people even higher up to almost 193 million people in 2021 GRFC 2022. With the onset of the war in Ukraine in early 2022 global acute food insecurity rose again in 2022 with as many as 205 million people in Phase 3 crisis or higher food insecurity as of September 2022 GRFC MidYear Update.

title.narrative: Output 1: Reinforced partnerships for early warning and early action systems

description.narrative: The FSP will contribute to reinforce the Food Security Information Network (FSIN) and the Global Network Against Food Crises (GNAFC). In partnership with the FSIN, the FSP is expanded and enhanced as a hub for early warning and early action systems. It will address and build resilience to food crises by providing rapid access to the most relevant early warning tools to assess the impacts of global economic and weather shocks and policy shifts on FSN in the short and longer term, enabling affected and likely affected populations to be identified and food crises monitored. Accordingly, through the FSIN, the FSP will also contribute to the annual preparation of the Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC) and provide evidence and analyses on the causes of food crises in support of the work of the GNAFC.

title.narrative: Existence of a hub for early warning systems that is coordinated with FSIN

description.narrative: Existence of a hub for early warning systems that is coordinated with FSIN

comment.narrative: One at initial stageThe Global FSP has created a page that compiles the early warning tools of various organizations.

TargetOne userfriendly hubThe Global FSP and the FSP for Africa South of the Sahara has a comprehensive and userfriendly panel hub combining various sources of information that may affect food crises.Progress2019 Hub for early warning systems developed and live on the FSP. Control panel developed and live on the FSP.2020 COVID19 monitoring included in the control panel2021 further improvements made

The hub for early warning systems was developed and went live on the FSP in 2019. A control panel for risk monitoring was included. Further improvements where made in 2020 and 2021 e.g. COVID19 monitoring was added to the control panel.

title.narrative: Output 1: Reinforced partnerships for early warning and early action systems

description.narrative: The FSP will contribute to reinforce the Food Security Information Network (FSIN) and the Global Network Against Food Crises (GNAFC). In partnership with the FSIN, the FSP is expanded and enhanced as a hub for early warning and early action systems. It will address and build resilience to food crises by providing rapid access to the most relevant early warning tools to assess the impacts of global economic and weather shocks and policy shifts on FSN in the short and longer term, enabling affected and likely affected populations to be identified and food crises monitored. Accordingly, through the FSIN, the FSP will also contribute to the annual preparation of the Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC) and provide evidence and analyses on the causes of food crises in support of the work of the GNAFC.
